_about: Artwork for the site. Each entry names Wikimedia Commons files or Wikipedia articles (the lead image is used), tried in order; tools/site/fetch_art.py downloads them into assets/art/ and records credits, and the Fetch artwork workflow runs it on GitHub when this file changes. The remaining fields are the caption shown on the site: artist, title, date, place, a note on why the image was chosen, the focal point for cropping (CSS object-position), and an optional crop box [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions, used to trim scan margins.

wiki: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
home.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
home.note: A lone figure looks out over a landscape he can only partly see. Epistemology starts in the same place: with what we can make out, and what the fog still hides.

guide.title: The Astronomer
guide.note: A scholar reaches for a celestial globe with a book open beside him: learning from books and learning from the world in a single gesture.

map.title: Planisphaerium Copernicanum, from Harmonia Macrocosmica
map.note: Cellarius's atlas of the heavens set rival models of the cosmos side by side. The concept map does the same for rival theories of knowledge.

audio.title: His Master's Voice
audio.note: Nipper the dog, said to be listening to a recording of his late master's voice: perhaps the most famous picture of listening ever painted.

ch01.title: The Geographer
ch01.note: A scholar pauses over his charts, dividers in hand, and looks up as if struck by a thought. This chapter draws the map of the field.

ch02.title: The Death of Socrates
ch02.place: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
ch02.note: Condemned for impiety and for corrupting the young, Socrates keeps arguing until he takes the hemlock. The history of the theory of knowledge begins with his questions.

wiki: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
ch03.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
ch03.note: Dr Tulp lays bare the muscles of the forearm while his audience leans in to see. An argument can be dissected the same way, layer by layer.

ch04.title: The Tower of Babel
ch04.note: The builders' great project collapses once they can no longer understand one another's words. Many arguments fail the same way.

ch05.title: Melencolia I
ch05.note: A winged genius sits among instruments of measurement (compass, scale, hourglass, magic square), stalled before a question she cannot yet answer. What, exactly, is knowledge?

file: Giovanni Battista Piranesi - Le Carceri d'Invenzione - Second Edition - 1761 - 07 - The Drawbridge.jpg
Giovanni Battista Piranesi - Le Carceri d'Invenzione - First Edition - 1750 - 07 - The Drawbridge.jpg
Giovanni Battista Piranesi - Le Carceri d'Invenzione - Second Edition - 1761 - 14 - The Gothic Arch.jpg
ch06.title: The Drawbridge, plate VII of the Imaginary Prisons (Carceri d'invenzione)
ch06.note: Stairs lead to further stairs and bridges to further bridges, and nothing seems to rest on the ground. Piranesi drew the regress problem as architecture.

ch07.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
ch07.note: Above the mirror van Eyck wrote Johannes de eyck fuit hic, “Jan van Eyck was here,” and the mirror shows the room as a witness saw it: perception and testimony in one picture.

ch08.title: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas
ch08.note: Thomas will not believe until he has touched the wound: the skeptic's demand for evidence, taken literally.

ch09.title: Impression, Sunrise
ch09.note: The sun has risen every morning so far. Hume asked what, exactly, entitles us to expect that it will rise tomorrow.

wiki: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
ch10.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
ch10.note: A travelling lecturer pumps the air out of a flask to show what happens to a bird without it: science as public demonstration, dramatic, persuasive and not without cost.

ch11.title: Earthrise
ch11.note: The Earth seen from lunar orbit: as close as anyone had come to what the philosopher Thomas Nagel called the view from nowhere.

ch12.title: The School of Athens
ch12.note: Plato and Aristotle at the centre, surrounded by generations of thinkers in conversation and dispute: knowledge as something a community builds together.

wiki: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
ch13.title: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
ch13.place: stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston, in 1990
ch13.note: A ship in a storm recalls William Clifford's shipowner, who let an unseaworthy vessel sail because he had talked himself into believing it was safe.

wiki: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters
ch14.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters, plate 43 of Los Caprichos
ch14.note: When reason sleeps, owls and bats crowd in. The psychology of reasoning studies what fills the space when careful thought switches off.

wiki: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
The Cheat with the Ace of Clubs
ch15.title: The Cardsharps
ch15.note: An accomplice reads the young man's cards and signals, while the cheat reaches behind his back for a hidden card. Fallacies are tricks of the same kind, played with arguments.

ch16.title: The Ambassadors
ch16.note: Two envoys stand among the instruments of their age (globes, sundials, a lute), while a stretched skull resolves only when you change your point of view: an emblem for a toolkit.

ch17.title: The Librarian
ch17.note: A portrait assembled entirely from books: the right emblem for a glossary.

ch18.title: The Bookworm
ch18.note: High on a library ladder, a scholar reads with a book under each arm and another between his knees. Begin with one book at a time.

elephant.title: Blind Monks Examining an Elephant
elephant.note: Each monk touches one part and describes a different animal. The concept map offers twelve such angles on a single question.

cave.artist: Jan Saenredam, after Cornelis van Haarlem
cave.title: Plato's Cave
cave.note: Prisoners take shadows on a wall for reality: philosophy's oldest image of the gap between appearance and knowledge.
